figures.caption: Figure 5: Joint multi-task trade-off between website and persona accuracy as a function of the persona loss weight λ. Increasing λ dramatically improves persona accuracy (from ≈ 45% to ≈ 80%) while only gradually reducing website accuracy (from ≈ 90% to ≈ 75%).
Table 1: Canonical personas used in closed-set experiments (P1–P15). We denote the open-world class by OW, which aggregates additional unseen personas (Section 2).

Figure 1: Website fingerprinting baseline: per-site accuracy and macro-F1 of the site-only classifier across all ten target websites using 1,000-packet windows. All sites achieve high accuracy (typically 90%−95%), indicating that the encoder hθ learns strong discriminative features from packet metadata alone.

Figure 2: Per-site persona fingerprinting: macro-F1 for each of the fifteen canonical personas and the OW label on all ten websites. Each subfigure corresponds to one site, with the red horizontal line indicating overall persona accuracy on that site. Despite observing only 1,000-packet windows and no application payload, the attacker can reliably distinguish personas within each website.
